artworks.title: Technical drawings and documents relating to the British Mint
artworks.description: A collection of 25 engineering drawings, sketches, notes and scale cards, related to the design of the British Mint at Tower Hill in London. The works are drawn on artist's paper, plain paper, tissue, cardboard and re-used printed paper in ink, pencil and colour wash. The group comprises the following:

artworks.title: Engineering drawing of the British Mint by Boulton Watt and Co.
artworks.description: The plan is drawn within a frame and has the drawing code ITH followed by 'copy' written in the top left corner. The code IWC is written below ITH.

artworks.title: Sketch of annealing furnaces at British Mint
artworks.description: This sketch is headed 'Anneal'g Furnaces for Dies' and dated 26 October 1805. It includes a plan and front elevation of two furnaces (with two others partially drawn in the elevation) and is drawn on the back of a pre-1800 Boulton & Watt contract that refers to the annual premium to be paid for an engine. The date, some dimensions and the names of some parts (column and iron bar) are written on the sketch. On the reverse, a different person probably sketched a barn and circles and repeatedly pra

artworks.title: Floor plan of milling and annealing apartments for British Mint
artworks.description: This ink sketch has no title, frame or scale. Compared to the General Plan 87/654-1, it is drawn upside down and contains more information on the room labelled 'Shaking from [hot]'. The room on the left is labelled 'Milling'. A door from there to the right leads to the 'Shaking' room, at one end of which are two dotted rectangles, one labelled 'Machines', presumably designed to shake coin blanks, with two other structures between them; at the other end of this room is the word 'Stove', which was

artworks.title: Sketch of recoil damper at British Mint
artworks.description: This is a small ink sketch on a corner torn from a sheet of paper. It is headed 'recoil damper pipe BM' and shows a cylindrical wooden damper that almost fills an open-ended horizontal pipe. The end of the damper that extends beyond the pipe has a narrow section ending in a disc that is too big to fit within the pipe.

artworks.title: Signed sketch of circles by Matthew Boulton
artworks.description: This rough pencil sketch is headed by Matthew Boulton's signature. It consists of circles of different sizes, straight lines and a curved vertical pipe that ends in a narrow section fitted with a stopcock. There are some numbers and calculations and the word 'under' appears twice. Some circles are concentric and there are six pairs of small circles that abut each other and could represent rollers for squeezing metal strips to make them thinner.

artworks.title: Sketch of shaking stove for British Mint
artworks.description: This ink sketch is headed 'Sketch of Stove for Shakeing'. Beside this is written in pencil: 'Sent to Mr Rennie July 1808'.

artworks.title: Scale used by Matthew Boulton
artworks.description: This hand-drawn 10-inch cardboard scale has 100 divisions marked in ink along the top edge, with numbers in tens from 0 to 100 written beneath the appropriate divisions. Below are written 'Scale of Feet' in one hand, and '1/10 of an Inch to a foot' (1:120) in another hand.

artworks.title: Scale used by Matthew Boulton
artworks.description: A hand-drawn scale sits centrally on a cardboard strip; it is marked in ink with unit divisions from -10 to 0 and from there to 100 by tens, with 200 marked on the right hand end; the scale is surrounded by a thick black frame, below which the division lines are extended to the bottom edge of the strip so it could be used for direct measurement of lengths on a plan. Above is written 'SCALE of FEET'. No scale is stated, but 1 inch represents 15 feet, so the scale is 1:180.

artworks.title: Floor plan of British Mint by Matthew Boulton
artworks.description: The engine room is shown at the right, and from there towards the left follow apartments for cutting out and milling coin blanks; tubing (which might have meant placing batches of distorted blanks in tubes for transfer to a press that flattened them all at the same time), annealing (softening the metal so its surface can be re-shaped in the coining press) and then pickling (written mistakenly as 'picking') the coin blanks in dilute sulphuric acid to remove copper oxide from their surfaces; shaki

artworks.title: Conceptual floor plan for new building at British Mint
artworks.description: Machines for rolling metal are roughly sketched in the right-hand apartment, along with the pencil annotation '& Reverbatory Furnaces' (a reverberatory furnace being one in which the fuel is not in contact with the substance to be heated). From there towards the left follow a 'Double Engine House', and then apartments for: cutting out & milling (with two concentric circles pencilled in, probably to suggest the arrangement of cutting-out presses and the overhead wheel that activated them via cams

artworks.title: Engineering drawing of lathes for the British Mint
artworks.description: The title at the top of this drawing is written in ink: 'Sketch of the Method of turning the lathe over the milling room'. Beside this is written 'British Mint' and '1/3 Inch to the foot', a scale of 1:36. The drawing is framed and has the code JMT at top left.

artworks.title: Scale card for rolling mill room at British Mint
artworks.description: Handwritten in black ink on the front of this card are 'Rolling Mill' and the room's dimensions, 53 feet 4 inches by 43 feet 4 inches. On the back of the card is written 'No 7'. This card represents the room in the mint where rolling machines squeezed strips of metal to the required thickness before coin blanks were cut from them.

artworks.title: Scale card for British Mint engine house
artworks.description: Handwritten in black ink on the front of this card are 'Double Steam Engine House' and the room's dimensions, 33 feet 4 inches by 43 feet 4 inches. On the back of the card is written 'No 8'. This card represents the room in the mint that would house the double-acting six-column steam engine to power the rolling mill, or perhaps 'double' indicates that it would hold two steam engines, one to power the rolling mill and the other to power the cutting-out presses.

artworks.title: Scale card for Picking and Weighing apartment at British Mint
artworks.description: Handwritten in black ink on the front of this card are 'Picking & Weighing' and the room's dimensions, 27 feet 4 inches by 43 feet 4 inches. On the back of the card is written 'No 11'. This card represents the apartment in the mint where all blanks were weighed and randomly selected examples were 'pyxed', that is, placed in a small box known as a pyx (a name borrowed from church practice) to be retained for official inspection.

artworks.title: Folder made by Matthew Boulton for British Mint scale cards
artworks.description: A sheet of paper with three parallel creases. It is labelled in ink, twice in the same hand: 'British Mint Apartments'.

artworks.title: Sketch of wells for the British Mint by Boulton Watt & Co
artworks.description: This ink sketch shows the planned positions of the cooling-water wells in the British Mint. Measurements and notations are written in ink. There are rough sketches on the reverse.

artworks.title: Drawing of milling machine at British Mint
artworks.description: Two ink sketches, with measurements also noted in ink, sit within a ruled ink frame. The drawing is coded JJA in the top left corner.

artworks.title: Sketch of clamps at the British Mint
artworks.description: This is a rough sketch, in ink and pencil, of some clamps and other structures. There are other pencil sketches on the reverse.

artworks.title: Sketch of additional apartments at the British Mint
artworks.description: The drawings on this L-shaped piece of paper, cut from a Boulton & Watt contract, are indistinct.

artworks.title: Plan of rolling mill for the British Mint
artworks.description: The drawing is headed 'Plan No 1' and shows a plan view of equipment, probably a rolling mill for the British Mint. Below this is a list of gear wheel sizes and their numbers of teeth, from 12 feet diameter with 130 teeth and 10 feet diameter with 110 teeth, to wheels of unstated diameter but with 43, 96, 86 and 48 teeth. Beside the list of teeth are other numbers, probably the number of that size wheel required.

artworks.title: Notes on the proportion of colours in sunlight by Matthew Boulton
artworks.description: The heading 'Sun - Proportion of Colours' is written in ink on this page, with red, green, blue and white listed below, with numbers beside them. The word 'colours' was first written as 'coulours', but the first u was crossed out. There are similar lists and calculations written in pencil elsewhere on the page.

artworks.title: Architectural drawing of British Mint coining room

artworks.title: Architectural drawing of British Mint coining room

Located in this area is a bulldozer, man with saxophone, chicken and dog.

artworks.title: Collection of Hedda Morrison photographs
artworks.medium: black and white silver gelatin print
artworks.description: The photographs document the landscape, customs, lifestyles, architecture, local traditions and craft practices of the people of Asia.

artworks.title: 'Kashmiri women outside a mosque in Srinagar' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a crowd of women, wearing head veils, sitting in the foreground. In front of the mosque (in the middleground of the photograph), a crowd of men, wearing turbans, is seated. The mosque building has a decorative facade, carved with various motifs around wide lancet windows. Its tiered roof is overgrown by grass.

artworks.title: 'Young apprentice in a papermaking workshop' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a young boy, dressed in trousers and cotton shirt brushing wet sheets of coarse hand made paper onto an external wall of the workshop to dry. To his left, paper sheets in various stages of the drying process being to peel off the wall. A wheelbarrow, laden with stacks of paper, is behind and to the left of the boy.

artworks.title: 'Itinerant barber' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a street barber shaving a young man's head in a park. The barber stands behind the seated man, running a razor over the back of his head. The customer holds a plate of hair shavings. The barber's travelling wash stand is at the right of the image and an empty rickshaw is stationed behind the men. In the background, another barber stands with his back to the camera, wearing a long jacket and fur cap. A second rickshaw lays idle on the ground, suggesting the men

artworks.title: 'Paper making by the traditional method' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man at a paper slurry tray drawing up the paper onto a bamboo frame. The man stands in a pit which allows him to work more easily and wears a protective work apron. Behind him are piles of finished paper.

artworks.title: 'Looking towards the Western Hills from Tuancheng Yanwuting' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a view taken of the valley towards the Western Hills (Xishan). Cultivated fields can be seen in the foreground. A pagoda and tombs surrounded by a wall are in the middleground. In the distance, hills and plantations can be seen.

artworks.title: 'Man selling persimmons outside Tiananmen' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man seated on a bench with baskets of persimmon fruits in front of him. Trees and a stone bridge leading to Tiananmen Gate, one of the gates within the Forbidden City, can be seen in the background.

artworks.title: 'Man and children enjoying the winter sunshine' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man and two children enjoying the winter sunshine. The man is seated on the edge of a large basket smoking a pipe. Two children are beside him in the basket - one seated, the other standing to the right of the image, touching the man on his back. All are dressed in warm padded clothes. The man wears a hat with ear flaps.

artworks.title: 'Hard wood furniture maker using a traditional drill' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a furniture maker seated outdoors at a small table and working on a wooden box using a traditional wooden drill, shaped like a cross. A small hammer lies on top of the box.

artworks.title: 'A corner of the Forbidden City wall and moat' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing two boys stand at the edge of a moat surrounding the Forbidden City or Imperial Palace. A heavily pruned willow tree is at the right of the image in the foreground and another tree with full hanging branches and leaves frames the top of the image. People are walking along or fishing from a low wall on the far side of the moat and a higher wall sits behind it. Behind the high outer wall we can see the roof of a palace within the palace grounds. After the collaps

artworks.title: 'Wood worker' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.medium: 'Wood worker' paper / silver gelatin / card / metal
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a woodworker seated in a workshop making the shaft of a crossbow. He is using a curved tool to shape the shaft. One foot presses on the base of the shaft, holding it in place. Numerous tools can be seen hanging on the wall of the workshop behind.

artworks.title: 'Second-hand goods seller at Tianqiao market' photograph my Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man squatting outside with an array of metalware spread on the ground in front of him, and furniture, such as chairs, behind him. In the background are buildings and two more men who are also selling goods.

artworks.title: 'Man with a hand drum selling needles and sewing thread' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing an elderly man crouching in front of a box of thread on a dirt road, holding a hand drum in his right hand which he uses to advertise his wares. Inside the lid of the box, a slogan has been written in Chinese characters ('A sea of wine, a mountain of meat' implying an abundance of these luxury goods). In the background a brick wall can be seen with ceramic pots piled up against it.

artworks.title: 'Working Laquer' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.medium: 'Working Laquer' paper / silver gelatin / card / metal
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing two young men at a table, one seated and one standing, carve lacquer boxes. Carved boxes and tools are spread on the table and more boxes are piled on a table in the background. A man peers through a window at the right of the image.

artworks.title: 'The Bell Tower' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a view of the Bell Tower (a two-storeyed square tower in brick with a tiled roof) from the Drum Tower. Rooftops can be seen to the right of the tower and a market under tents is in the left foreground. Plains extend behind the tower in the distance.

artworks.title: 'Looking back to Coal Hill from the wall of the Forbidden City' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a view across the moat surrounding the Forbidden City with the wall of the Palace in the foreground. On the far side of the moat there are two pavillions surrounded by a wall. Two buildings sit atop Coal Hill in the distance to the right of the image.

artworks.title: 'The Forbidden City' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a view of the Forbidden City from above, across rooftops. The outline of mountains can be seen in the far distance.

artworks.title: 'Checking the balance of Chinese scales' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a young boy standing at a table checking the balance of scales. He is wearing an apron and stands in front of a woodwork table. On the wall beside him, to the left of the image, a calligraphic Chinese couplet hang on the wall.

artworks.title: 'Young woman from the outer suburbs of Peking with a Southern Chinese style hairstyle' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing close-up of a young girl in profile. The girl's long hair has been pulled back in a decorative ponytail, doubled back on itself - the section tied at the base of her neck and bound with a cord. She has an earring in her ear and her eyes are averted.

artworks.title: 'Young acrobat at Tianqiao market' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a young boy balancing on a stool with a tier of bowls on his head. A crowd behind looks on.

artworks.title: 'Pot market outside the north-east gate' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a pot market outside the north-east gate of the Chinese City wall. There are leafless trees in the fore, middle and background. Ceramic pots are stacked up at different points. An arched gate in the background leads into the Chinese City. A number of people are walking or pulling rickshaws through the archway. To the right and left of the gate are low buildings with tiled roofs.

artworks.title: 'Decorative street signs for a cake shop' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a view of intricately carved wooden shop signs. The signs use attributes of the Taoist Immortals, each of whom was commonly associated with a particular item. For instance, the lotus and the fly whisk (bottom sign), the crutch and the gourd (third sign down), the fan and the flywhisk, and the ribbon and the cloud. The links between each sign refer to Buddha ('Buddha's hand upon peach').

artworks.title: 'Rickshaws' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing an aerial view in the centre of which two rickshaw pullers can be seen with their rickshaws. A third rickshaw is in the bottom left corner of the image, with its puller out of view. A woman leading a small child can be seen in the top left corner. The two rickshaws in the centre cast long shadows in front of them.

artworks.title: 'Street scene in the outer Chinese city' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a narrow busy street in the Chinese city of Peking with many banners hanging from shopfronts. Three rickshaw pullers pull rickshaws up the street beside pedestrians. Other pedestrians browse in shopfront windows.

artworks.title: 'Outside the south-east corner watchtower of the inner city wall during a dust storm' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a group of people caught in a dust storm. Two people carrying a load between them on a shoulder pole can be seen in the centre of the image, along with other people and rickshaws. A small shed-like structure can be seen behind them, as well as trees and the southeast corner watchtower. The watchtower is part of the city walls that once defined the city of Peking. In their present form the walls date from the Ming Dynasty (1421-1439), but their history can be tr

artworks.title: 'Funeral procession' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing view from the top of a city wall, with a view of the street below with a large number of mourners in a funeral procession. The mourners are led by people dressed in white and followed by elaborately dressed men carrying a decorated bier. Carts, cars and pedestrians travel on both sides of the road. From the city wall, you can see the rooftops of the low level city buildings stretching into the distance.

artworks.title: 'Spinning silk' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man spinning silk floss into thread. Only the upper body of the man is visible. He is holding a frame on which there are eight spindles of thread. Each spindle has thread wound onto it. He is possibly making silk rope (sidi). The process of spinning thread required a large, open space. In this instance, an area outside the city wall has been chosen, indicated by the high brick wall that can be seen behind the spinner.

artworks.title: 'Feather duster seller' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man in winter clothes, wearing a fur cap and layers of clothing, holding feather dusters. The dusters are made of chicken feathers, mounted on wooden poles. The man's cloth purse hangs from his left shoulder.

artworks.title: 'Qianmen Boulevard and the memorial archway at Zhengyang Bridge after snowfall' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a street corner following a snowfall. The image has been taken from above and looks down over a street corner. A camel train crosses the street in the foreground (the camels are transporting coal) and pedestrians travel the road in both directions, pushing carts and pulling rickshaws. There are two trees and a portion of a third tree covered in snow in the foreground and snow covers the footpath and electricity poles. Tram tracks traverse the street and the sce

artworks.title: 'Funeral procession at the foot of Zhengyang Gate Watchtower' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing symbolic paper money being thrown before a funeral bier and can be seen falling through the air and lying on the ground. A man in a white robe and dark cap stands in the front right corner with his hands clasped in front of him. Following him is another group of men in white, followed by an elaborately decorated bier which is being carried by a large group of men. Each of the carriers wears a dark gown decorated with white circles. The corner of the Zhengyang G

artworks.title: 'Roadside fortune teller' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man seated on a step, reading, behind him the wall of a building. Spread before him are fortune telling paraphernalia, including books, I Ching wheel, inscriptions, an open folder of painted watercolours, a framed picture, fortune sticks, beads and incense. The photograph has been dry mounted onto white card with reinforced corner punches.

artworks.title: 'Assembling glass grapes' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing two women seated at table assembling bunches of glass grapes. A window can be seen behind them.

artworks.title: 'Making copper wire' photrograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man at a hand operated windlass drawing wire. There are coils of wire hanging from the walls of the room and leaning against the windlass post.

artworks.title: 'Making glass grapes' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man at a hand operated windlass drawing wire. There are coils of wire hanging from the walls of the room and leaning against the windlass post.

artworks.title: 'Roasting Peking duck at the Quanjude Restaurant' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man facing a brick oven. He holds a pole, from which hangs a duck that he is roasting inside the mouth of the oven.

artworks.title: 'Chinese New Year painting and calligraphy stall, Haiwang Village, east of Liulichang' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing three men wearing hats and padded robes standing in front of an outdoor stall viewing a Chinese painting hanging from a wall.

artworks.title: 'Stupa within the Yellow Temple' photograph by hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a view along a columned portico, a terrace and stairs to the left of the portico. The roof beams and ceiling panels of the portico are richly carved and painted. At the far end of the portico hangs a large bell. The Temple is situated in the north-east of present-day Beijing.

artworks.title: 'View through a moon gate from Qionghua Island in Beihai towards the Bell and Drum Towers' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing view northwards through a moon gate below the Beihai Pagoda on Hortensia Island ('Qiong hua dao'). The Bell and Drum Towers can be seen in the distance. The moon gate frames the scene. The North Sea Lake is one of three lake parks in Peking where emperors built palaces and summer pleasences. It is said to date back to the Jin Dynasty (1115-1234), when waters from springs in the western hills were diverted here. The Lake was favoured by the Manch-Qing emperors K

artworks.title: 'Burning incense to the city god at the Chenghuang Temple' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a crowd of people burning incense and offerings before a brick furnace at Chenghuang Temple.

artworks.title: 'Huazang Pagoda at Jade Spring Hill' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a view of a misty lake in the foreground with pavilions on the other side of the lake. A wooded hill rises behind the buildings and the Huazang pagoda.

artworks.title: 'Coal Hill after snowfall' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a landscape dotted with buildings and covered in snow. The corner of a tiled roof and the branches of a tree can be seen in the foreground. A wall and buildings covered with snow are in the middle ground and a pavillion can be seen sitting atop a hill in the distance.

artworks.title: 'Selling persimmons' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a young girl sitting on a small stool by the side of a street with a mat in front of her, on which piles of persimmons are arranged for sale. Beside her to the left of the image is a cart, also piled with fruit. Two people inspect fruit on the cart. Pedestrians and rickshaws can be seen in the background. Buildings line the far side of the street.

artworks.title: 'Bird fancier' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing an old man seated on a bank of dirt, looking at a small bird in cage on the ground to his right (at left of frame). The man has a long beard and wears a long, fur-lined robe and a skull cap. Bare trees can be seen in the background.

artworks.title: 'Pagodas at Jade Spring Hill' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a wall in the foreground on the left of the image. Behind this, two carved pagodas can be seen rising up behind a tree on the far side of the wall. The pagoda closest to the wall has three tiers, divided by paired tiled overhangs. Above each pair of overhangs is a balcony. The pagoda has a tiled roof on top, surmounted by a pair of bell-shaped devices. To the right of the image on the near side of the wall a grassy hill slopes upwards.

artworks.title: 'Altar of the Daoist Baiyun guan Temple' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing view from behind the altar of the Taoist temple (Baiyun guan) looking out onto the temple courtyard. The darkness of the temple interior causes the candle stands and offerings on the altar to appear in silhouette. The central candle stand is ornamented by a deer, a Taoist symbol. A bronze censer stands in the courtyard and there is a view beyond to the building in the distance.

artworks.title: 'Imperial gateway to the Temple of Heaven' photograph by Hedda Morisson
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a view through the southern entrance of the Temple of Heaven, Tiantan, looking towards Qinian dian (Hall of Annual Prayers). The view is through carved, white, marble gateways, the wooden doors of which are propped open with stones. The pathway leads to the Temple of Heaven, the roof of which can be seen in the distance.

artworks.title: 'The Altar of Heaven in moonlight' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing the view from the lower terrace of the Altar of Heaven ('Huan Qiu') of shadows, cast by moonlight, of the upper terrace railing. Three marble gateways, the centre one with gates open, the outer ones with gates closed, are set in an enclosing circular wall. Beyond them and the wall, the tops of three marble gateways leading to the Temple of Heaven can be seen. In the background, trees are silhouetted against the horizon.

artworks.title: 'Looking towards the Summer Palace from Yuquan Mountain' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing 'a view to the Summer Palace taken from Jade Spring Mountain (Yuquan shan). The view is across irrigated rice paddies to hills and the Summer Palace in the distance.

artworks.title: 'Bringing home good fortune' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing the head and torso of a young girl, her head turned to her right (to the left of frame). She is dressed in a knitted jumper and striped skirt. Decorations made from chenille are pinned to her jumper and ornament her hair. She is framed by a masonry archway in the background.

artworks.title: 'North-west corner tower of the outer city wall' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a train of camels moving from the left to the right of the image in the snow. The camel train crosses in front of the outer city wall. A corner tower is positioned at the centre of the image and trees frame the foreground. The ground is covered in snow.

artworks.title: 'Street puppet theatre' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man, a woman and five children watching a puppet show. The show is mounted in a miniature theatre on the street in front of a wall to the right of the image. The man and the children grin at the female puppet propped up inside the theatre box. A woman stands with them holding a baby in her arms. The female puppet has a painted ceramic face and wears a beaded and embroidered headdress.

artworks.title: 'Broom peddler' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a young man in a fur hat pushing cart of brooms. The young man carries a stick and is striking a gourd to attract customers. Behind him is a wall on which graffitti in Chinese characters can be seen.

artworks.title: 'Jade polishing workshop' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man with a piece of jade at a polishing machine. A cup and dish also sit on the machine bench. The man's arm leans across the machine to polish the jade.

artworks.title: 'Traditional musical instruments being played at a funeral' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing two musicians standing in a street, performing at a funeral procession. Each musician is wearing a white cone-shaped hat and a robe decorated with white dots which form circular motifs, a design that was used on funeral garments. One musician is playing a long horn, the other a large drum which is slung over his shoulder with rope. A doorway can be seen in the background. These musicians form part of a funeral procession photographed by Hedda Morrison. There ar

artworks.title: 'Rickshaw puller having a nap' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a close-up of a rickshaw puller's face as he sleeps. The puller is resting his head against his rickshaw as he has a nap in the sun. The wheel of his rickshaw can be seen at the left of the image.

artworks.title: 'Young boy' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a close-up of a boy child in a striped shirt. His head is shaved except for a knot of hair on his forehead. He is seated between the knees of an adult.

artworks.title: 'Female artist' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a female artist standing before a table in her studio. A large Chinese landscape painting hangs behind her. She wears a cheongsam and is standing with both hands placed on the table looking into the camera. On the table, in front of her to her left (right of frame), is a brush pot, brush washer and porcelain dish for mixing colours.

artworks.title: 'Young boy' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a child whose hair is in pigtails. He is wearing a shirt buttoned to his neck and his pigtails are wrapped in string. His hands are visible at the bottom of the image and he is wearing a ring on the middle finger of her left hand.

artworks.title: 'Young lama from Yonghe Temple' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.medium: 'Young lama from Yonghe Temple' paper / silver gelatin / card / metal
artworks.description: Photograph, black and white, 'Young lama from Yonghe Temple' paper / silver gelatin / card / metal, photographed by Hedda Morrison, Peking, China, 1933-1946.

artworks.title: 'Daoist monk from Baiyunguan Temple' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Photograph, black and white, 'Daoist monk from Baiyunguan Temple', paper / silver gelatin / card / metal, photographed by Hedda Morrison, Peking, China, 1933-1946.

artworks.title: Buddhist monk making an offering photograph by Heda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a monk making an offering at an altar in a Buddhist temple. Dressed in a long robe, with a shaven head, he is holding up a bowl in front of the altar. On the altar are two large candle holders and various metal vessels. The altar is situated in a large hall with columns. Couplets carved into the wood adorn the columns.

artworks.title: 'Abbott' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a portrait of a Buddhist abbot wearing a loose, pale-coloured robe and dark framed glasses. He has a shaved head. The abbot is seated at a table, a book in front of him and holding a Buddhist rosary in his left hand.

artworks.title: 'Road on the outskirts of Peking' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man leading a horse which is pulling a covered wagon on a country track. The view is from above and tracks can be seen leading either side of a stand of trees near the centre of the image. Two figures walking on the track can be seen to the left of the trees. More trees can be seen through the mist in the background.

artworks.title: 'Flowering plum blossom at Zhongnan hai' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a carved marble balustrade in the foreground and a wall in the background. A flowering plum blossom tree stands along a pathway between the balustrade and the wall.

artworks.title: 'Looking north towards Taihe Hall inside the Forbidden City' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a view across a grassed courtyard to a three-tiered marble terrace leading up to Taihe Hall.

artworks.title: 'Detail of mural painting at Fahai Temple' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing detail of mural painting.

artworks.title: 'Balizhuang Pagoda' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Photograph, 'Balizhuang Pagoda', black and white, paper / silver gelatin / card / metal , photographed by Hedda Morrison, Peking, China, 1933-1946.

artworks.title: 'Cloisonné enamel workshop' photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Photograph, black and white, 'Cloisonné enamel workshop', paper / silver gelatin / card / metal, photographed by Hedda Morrison, Peking, China, 1933-1946.

artworks.title: 'Daoist musician playing multi-toned gongs at a funeral'
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a Daoist musician playing gongs. The musician, a male in dressed in a Daoist robe and wearing a cap, is holding a frame in his left hand to which 10 gongs are tied. In his right hand he is holding a thin stick to strike the gongs. At the lower right of the image, three figures can be seen in the distance, out of focus.

artworks.title: 'Making a ceramic roof tile' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing the close up of an artisan's hands as he carves patterns in a ceramic tile for the corner of a roof. The tile is in the shape of an animal head.

artworks.title: 'Old man at a Chinese New Year stall, Liulichang' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a man in a brocade robe, vest and skull cap inspecting antiques at an open air stall. A tree stands behind him and the roof of a building can be seen in the background to the left.

artworks.title: 'Antiquarian bookshop' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a young man seated at a writing desk. He has a pen in his hand and is writing on a piece of paper. He is practicing the traditional Chinese calligraphy by copying the model of calligraphy copybook. The copybook, a piece of inkstone, an open ink box, a ceramic brush pot and a brush holder with two brushes hunging on it sit on the desk in front of him. Beside him, to the right of the man (left of the image) is a clock in a case and light streams in the window beh

artworks.title: 'Repairing an antique scroll prior to remounting' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a close up of a young man bending over a lacquered table, repairing an antique scroll prior to remounting.

artworks.title: 'Seller of coloured paper lanterns and whistles' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a street vendor selling whistles and paper lanterns. The man is wearing a robe and skull cap and has a whistle in his mouth to demonstrate the sound of the whistle. Paper lanterns are suspended in the top left hand corner of the image.

artworks.title: 'The artist Wang Qingfang painting, with children' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing the artist Wang Qingfang, painting with brush and ink on a drop-sided table as children play with books and manuscripts on the stone floor at his feet. A chair sits against the wall to the right of the frame. Paintings hang on the wall behind him.

artworks.title: 'Outer city gate after snowfall' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing bare winter snow-dusted trees screening a view of a corner of the outer city wall and a gate tower. The ground is covered in snow.

artworks.title: 'Playing Chinese chess' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing two young men wearing traditional Chinese dress seated on a heated platform ('kang') playing Chinese chess (Xiang qi). The 'kang' is decorated with wooden panelling and applied carved designs. To the left of the photograph, a decorative carved wooden screen frames the window and two rectangular window or mirror like panels are fixed to the wall above the 'kang'.

artworks.title: 'Spring fields on the outskirts of Peking' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing cultivated rice fields in springtime viewed from a high vantage point. A large tree stands in the foreground and more trees can be seen in the middle ground, with a few small farm buildings dotted among them.

artworks.title: 'Calligraphy and painting scroll mounting workshop' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing scroll mounters in the process of mounting scrolls on a large lacquered table. This image shows six young men around a table in a workshop in the process of mounting scrolls. Three men are at the right of the table and one is standing at the left of the table wearing an apron. Two are at the far end of the table, one of whom has his back to the photographer reaching to a large board onto which a scroll has been mounted and suspended from the ceiling to dry.

artworks.title: 'Camel train transporting coal from Mentougou in the Western Hills'
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a camel train trekking across a snow covered landscape from Mentougou in the Western Hills towards Peking. A camel and rider is in the foreground on the right of the image and the rest of the camel train can be seen winding along a curved path into the distance towards the city and the trees on the horizon line.

artworks.title: 'Paying respects at New Year' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph depicting a young boy kneeling before his family shrine with his back to the camera. His parents are seated on either side of the altar, their gaze directed at him. His father, wearing a long robe and a jacket (chang pao magua), is seated to the left and his mother, dressed in padded trousers and a jacket, is seated on the right of the image. Scrolls with Chinese decorations hang in the background.

artworks.title: 'Ritual procession of Buddhist nuns in the Western City' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a procession of nine Buddhist nuns, each carrying a musical instrument.

artworks.title: 'Young boy wearing a Mongolian hat' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing close-up of a young boy in a fur lined, embroidered hat. The boy is looking at the camera.

artworks.title: 'Detail of a mural at Fahai Temple' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a Ming fresco which show a man and two women in elaborate robes.

artworks.title: 'Kings' tombs on the outskirts of Peking' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing engraved stone stele and carved stone guardian animals which signify the location of the tombs of kings. There are small mounds of earth in the foreground, two large trees in the middle ground and a line of trees at the horizon line.

artworks.title: Silver gelatin print by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing view to the hills from within the overgrown grounds of the Eunuch's Temple. The view is framed by two trees. Just to the right of centre is a stone column surmounted by the figure of a lion ('huabiao') and there are two carved figures, one at bottom left, the other at lower right of the image. From the temple grounds you can see the rooftops of temple buildings in the middle-ground and terraced hills in the distance.

artworks.title: 'Ming tombs' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a view of the entrance to the precinct housing the tombs of the Ming emperors situated in open fields with mountains in the distance. The Tablet House stands in the middle ground flanked by a 'huabiao' column and two tall sculptures at either side. A spirit road flanked with carved stone guardian figures and animals leads to the tombs beyond.

artworks.title: Photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing two women sitting on the ground, surrounded by a confusing array of bowls and baskets, containing vegetables, fruit and leaves (which contain the betel nuts). Behind the women, a small child sits in a chair. Both women are wearing pale blouses and batik print skirts. The betel nut is the fruit of the betel palm (botanical name areca catehu). It is chewed with lime derived from burnt coral or shells and with any of a variety of hot substances, such as the leaves

artworks.title: 'Land Dayak woman in party dress' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing a close-up view of a woman. She is wearing a cotton felt dress, probably for the rice festival. Such material was imported from India or China. Around her neck are many strands of trade beads. Her cap is made of shaped material and trimmed with braid. It was only worn for special occasions, never for working in the fields.

artworks.title: Photograph by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing two men, each sitting at a potter's wheel, drawing clay. Beside them, pots have been arranged in rows on the ground. One of the potters sits under a woven shade structure. In the background is a cart wheel.

artworks.title: 'Indian Temple Orchestra' by Hedda Morrison
artworks.description: Black and white photograph showing five men seated on the ground in a temple courtyard. They are musicians, three playing shawms (type of pipe) and one playing a drum.

artworks.description: Watercolour on canvas backed paper in scale 3 to 1. The drawing shows a branch with green leaves highlighted with white, several brown leaves, a cluster of brown gumnuts and 6 clusters of white and green gum blossoms. The name of the species of the plant is underneath the drawing and it is signed by the artist in the lower left corner and near the end of the branch. All text is in black.

artworks.title: Photograph of a drawing of a 1785 Boulton and Watt beam engine
artworks.artist: Boulton and Watt for Whitbread's Brewery
artworks.description: A photograph reproduction showing a drawing of the beam engine made by Boulton and Watt for Whitbread and Company in London, England. The drawing is a finely detailed rendered image of the engine that is now in this Museum's collection. It shows the engine in its final form at the brewery, with some detail of the supporting timbers and safety railings. It also includes a cutaway view of the tank, revealing the separate condenser, air pump, hot well and dashpots. The photograph is mounted on card

artworks.title: Stereograph of men fishing
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show two men in a row boat on a river. The man at the front of the boat looks to be pulling a trap from the water. Trees can be seen lining the waters edge. There is handwritten text on the back of the image.

artworks.title: Stereograph of 'their sunlight-spotted trunks'
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show a man reclining on one elbow in the grass in front of a forest. The images have been tinted with the grass and foliage green and the scarf around the mans neck red. There is printed text on the front of the mount and handwritten text on the back of the mount.

artworks.title: Stereograph of men and women eating a meal
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two hand coloured images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show four women and two men seated around a dinner table. Two of the women's dresses have been hand coloured one pink, the other blue.There is a window in the background through which blue sky can be seen. The curtains around the window have been coloured green while the legs of the side table in the right of the image

artworks.title: Stereograph of church in Italy
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show a large building featuring towers, turrets and domes. The image has been taken from a distance viewed through trees and parkland. There is printed text on the front of the mount and handwritten text on the back of the mount.

artworks.title: Stereograph of women and men boating
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show three women who wear bonnets and are seated in a wooden punt. One man can be seen standing on the river bank and launching the boat, while another man can be seen trying to manoeuvre the boat with a long pole. There is printed text on the front of the mount and handwritten text on the back of the mount.

artworks.title: Stereograph of a 'Circassian Chief' statue
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show a statue of a Circassian chief who wears a hood and tunic. He holds a dagger in his right hand and what appears to be a rifle in his left hand. There is a dark curtain in the background. There is a printed label and handwritten text on the back of the mount.

artworks.title: Stereograph of oxen pulling agricultural machinery
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show a farmyard scene consisting of pairs of cows hitched to ploughs. A barn can be seen in the background. There are two printed labels on the front of the mount and handwritten initials on the back of the mount.

artworks.title: Stereograph of a group of girls
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two colour tinted black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show a group of six girls. The girl in the centre of the image is seated and surrounded by frame decorated with a garland of flowers. The frame is held by three girls who are standing. Two more girls kneel in front of the seated girl holding a posy of flowers. The girls dresses are tinted pink and the fl

artworks.title: Stereograph of 'The Children in the Wood'
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two colour tinted black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show two children, a boy and a girl, standing in a woodland setting. The girl wears a white dress with a full skirt and rubs her eye as if crying. The boy standing next to her has one arm around the girls shoulder and holds the girls hand. The boy wears short trousers with stockings and a tunic that butt

artworks.title: Stereograph of Moriston Falls, Scotland
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show a water fall on a fast moving river, the Morriston River in Scotland. Rocks can be seen protruding from the river. In the background is a stone bridge. There is printed handwritten text on the back of the mount and a stamp.

artworks.title: Stereograph of Venetian galley ship model
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show a model of a Venetian galley boat displayed on a table. The boat has a decoratively carved bow. Oars can be seen protruding from the body of the boat. There is printed text on the front of the mount and handwritten text on the back of the mount.

artworks.title: Stereograph of the 'Falls of the Clyde'
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show the Bonnington waterfalls that make up part of the River Clyde near New Lanark, Scotland. Several waterfalls can be seen. Rocks can be seen protruding from the surface of the water. The river banks are lined with trees. There is handwritten text on the back of the image.

artworks.title: Stereograph of 'Looking down Borrowdale, from the Bowder Stone'
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show the view of a rocky, tree lined valley. The is a printed label adhered to the back of the mount.

artworks.title: Stereograph of sundial at Dunkeld Cathedral
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show a view of a cathedral. Vines can be seen growing on the walls of the cathedral and a sun dial, fixed to an urn shaped plinth, can be seen in the garden in the foreground. The is a printed label adhered to the back of the mount.

artworks.title: Stereograph of 'Resignation' statue
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show a white [marble] statue of a seated woman. There is a printed label adhered to the back of the mount.

artworks.title: Stereograph of 'Holyrood Palace'
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show the forecourt and entrance to Holyrood Palace at the end of the Royal Mile in Edinburgh, Scotland. A wooden fence can be seen in the foreground of the image. The hills of Holyrood Park can be seen in the distance behind the palace. There is a printed label adhered to the back of the mount.

artworks.title: Stereograph of the 'The Knoll, Ambleside - the residence of Harriet Martineau'
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two colour tinted black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show the house of Harriet Martineau in the Lake District. The view of the two storey house has been taken from a distance. artworks.title: Stereograph of Klopp castle
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show the view across a field to the tower of a castle. Hills can be seen in the background of the image. Text has been printed on the front of the mount and there is handwritten text on the back of the mount.

artworks.title: Stereograph of 'The Llagwy at Tafy-Coed near Capel Curig, North Wales'

A river can be seen running through the valley and hills can be seen in the distance. The vegetation has been tinted green, the rocks and dry stone walls brown and the water blue. artworks.title: Stereograph of 'the gateway of the wood'
artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two colour tinted black and white images that have been taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show two men in an outdoor setting. One man stands on a pathway, the other is seated next to a stream. A fence with a gate in it can be seen in the background. Woodland can be seen behind the fence. There are handwritten initials on the back of the mount.

artworks.description: A stereoview photographic print consisting of two black and white images taken simultaneously. The prints have been mounted next to one another on a card. The images show the facade of the Otto Henry building in Heidelberg, Germany. The ornately decorated three storey facade features statues between the windows on each level. artworks.title: Bookplate design entitled 'Verandah Pillar, entablature and railing'
artworks.description: Illustrated bookplate showing a design for cast and enamelled iron verandah fittings. There is a column and architrave decorated with text, waratah flowers and classical leaf motifs with a dado featuring gold lyrebirds and a grey fish scale background and brick work at the top. There is also a design of cast iron lace with flannel flowers, a white cockatoo, scrolls and pierced disc to the right of the column. The background is plain black.

artworks.title: Bookplate design entitled 'Lyre-bird armchairs'
artworks.description: Illustrated bookplate for three views of a lyrebird armchair. The left chair is shown from behind, the centre chair is shown in profile and the right chair is shown from the front. They are decorated in blue, white and gold with waratah fabric covered seats There are three stenocarpus legs and stag-horn relief on the back of the chairs. The background comprises a dado panel with repeated waratah, seagull and wave motifs.

artworks.title: Photograph albums by Serge Vargassoff
artworks.dimensions: height 300 mm × width 420 mm × depth 47 mm
artworks.description: These five albums of photographs of China by Serge Vargassoff each contain approximately 1,000 photographs. The images show various landscape, architectural and genre scenes taken in and around Peking (Beijing), China. All five albums are landscape format and have thick cloth-covered cardboard covers. The pages of the albums are made of black card. They are bound on the left hand side with metal pinfastenings, some of which have been replaced with black string.

artworks.title: Poster, ' Mambo Etymology', by Reg Mombassa for Mambo Graphics
artworks.description: Title reads 'Mambo Etymology / The origin of crude sexual terms'. The comic format image of this poster is divided into five sexual vignettes derived from different locations around the world entitled 'The Pork Sword', 'The Hairy Harmonica', 'Crashing the Yogurt Truck' 'The Beef Curtain' and 'Mrs Hand and her Five Daughters'. Each is supplemented by Reg Mombassa text.

artworks.title: Recycling poster by The Body Shop
artworks.description: Portrait-format colour poster produced by The Body Shop to promote recycling. Twenty-five stylised illustrations of bottles bearing the company's logo are printed in bright colours above words beginning with the letters RE (for example reclaim, reuse, recharge, reuse, rethink, rebuild, reclaim, repair, recap, renew). The text 'Once is not enough' is printed across the across the bottom of the poster in black.

artworks.title: 'Reuse, Refill, Recycle' badge
artworks.description: Circular metal and plastic badge produced by The Body Shop to promote recycling. The badge features a stylised illustration of a green and blue bottle bearing the company's logo. The upper half of the badge is coloured pink and features the text 'Reuse, refill, recycle'. The lower half of the badge is coloured yellow. A lapel pin is attached to the back of the badge.

artworks.title: Pokerwork twenty-first birthday key
artworks.description: Plywood model of a key for celebrating twenty-first birthdays, decorated with a pokerwork design of green and red gumleaves. The key consists of a long shaft, one side of which has a notched edge like a door key. The top of the key (or the handle) has a circular ring which features the number 21 in the centre. The following text is burnt into the key's shaft: 'The Key to Success and Happiness'.

artworks.description: Monochrome digital photographic print depicting the interior of Patricia's Milk Bar, George Street, Wynyard, Sydney. Two women work at the counter which runs across the frame; a large geometric mural dominates the wall behind the counter. Samuel Lipson, designer of Patricia's Milk Bar in addition to several of Sydney's most prominent modernist structures, leans against the counter dressed in suit, hat and tie.

Two lines in the formation of a 'V' across the middle of the poster is centred by an Obama - Biden circular logo featuring Capitol Hill with text around the outside. Words 'BE THE CHANGE' are printed horizontally at the top of the poster and 'JANUARY 20TH 2009' is printed horizontally at the bottom of the poster. Words

artworks.title: Poster, 'We Have Survived'
artworks.description: The poster has the words 'We Have Survived' printed across the top, with the image of the Australian Indigenous flag overlaying the Australian coat of arms. 'Celebrate 60, 000 Years of Black Australian History' is printed down the left side of the above image, and 'Protest 200 Years of Oppression' is on the right. The bands No Fixed Address, Caribbe, and Tamatoa are advertised as playing at the Phoenician Club in Sydney on January 27 1985.

artworks.title: Indian cinema poster 'Hunterwali ki Beti'
artworks.dimensions: height 764 mm × width 512 mm × depth 1 mm
artworks.description: Portrait- format colour lithograph in yellow, blue and red. The field is divided into two main areas, the top two thirds being a montage of scenes from the film, as well as the names of the producer Homi Wadia and stars of the film, Fearless Nadia and her co-star John Cawas. The bottom third of the poster bears the title of the film 'Hunterwali Ki Beti' in English, Hindi and Urdu text, the name of the director, Batuk Bhatt and the logo of the film production company, Basant Pictures.

artworks.title: Indian cinema poster 'Hunterwali ki Beti'
artworks.dimensions: height 509 mm × width 765 mm × depth 1 mm
artworks.description: Landscape-format colour lithograph poster in green, orange and black. The field depicts a montage of scenes from the film, arranged around the central motif of a steam train speeding towards a woman tied to the train tracks. To the right of the train, prominence is given to a female figure, 'Fearless Nadia', dressed in masculine attire and holding a pistol. Other vignettes from the film include a fist fight and Moti the dog beside a man lying prone on the ground.

artworks.title: Photograph of Jocelyn Rickards by Alec Murray
artworks.description: This black & white photographic print depicts British-Australian costume designer Jocelyn Rickards. She is wearing a patterned dress and standing barefoot on a monument in a field (possibly a cemetery), with one hand raised to her forehead. A friend of Alec Murray, Jocelyn Rickards studied at a Sydney art school in the late 1930s and 1940s, before travelling to the UK in 1949 to work as a costume designer in numerous films.

artworks.title: Photographs of design for silk batik shawl featuring Byram Mansell's artwork
artworks.description: A similar Cazneaux photograph of the shawl appeared in an article, 'A Fantastic Chorus of Colour', in The Home magazine, 1 October 1925, where the shawl's colours were listed as 'burnished gold, henna, dull reds, purple and turquoise blue'. Described there as a Persian design, the shawl's caption, 'The Drehid', was possibly a misreading of 'The Orchid', as a Mansell shawl with the latter title was exhibited in the NSW Society of Arts and Crafts' annual exhibition held later in the same month.

artworks.title: Portrait of Shirley de Vocht by Hector Brown

artworks.title: Wall map of Sydney and Suburbs

It also shows the main ferry routes in Sydney Harbour and the surrounding waterways. The map extends as far north as Frenchs Forest and Harbord, south to Como, Sylvania and Weeney Bay and to Epping, Chullora and Peakhurst in the west, with Sydney's coast and the Tasman Sea to the east. artworks.description: Painting by Charmaine Green interpreting the western technologies used to receive radio signals at Murchison Widefield Array (MWA), which is located on Wajarri country. The painting has rough stripes of blue and black with coloured dots in the background. In the foreground are several circular shapes, each with four points emerging from the centre and representing the antennas.

artworks.title: Poster of photograph by James Wedge produced by Biba

The model wears a maroon felt pillbox hat, and a pair of Victoriana black lace fingerless gloves. She wears the signature Biba makeup style, pursed dark lip and smokey eyes.

artworks.title: 'Consumerism' by Michael Cook
artworks.description: Photograph entitled 'Consumerism', part of Individuation Series by Michael Cook. It depicts a man, Joey, standing in the centre of a street lined with designer store fronts. He is wearing Balenciaga garments and is accompanied by a horse eating from the iconic Balenciaga Chip handbag. On either side are multiple thin young men and women wearing high end luxury haute couture, ‘individuals’ mirrored with replicants. The streets are lined with brand names including Prada, Gucci, Dior, Louis Vuitton

artworks.title: 'Conformity' by Michael Cook
artworks.description: Photograph entitled 'Conformity', part of Individuation Series by Michael Cook. It depicts hundreds of replicants of a man, Joey, lining a cobbled street with London Bridge in the background. They are all dressed in a green Gucci suit. One man only wears the suit in yellow, yet all other details of his appearance are the same – it’s a minor rebellion. In the sky above a flock of birds fly in formation, echoing herd behaviour and drawing a parallel with our own animalistic need for conformity.

artworks.title: 'Attachment' by Michael Cook
artworks.description: Photograph entitled 'Attachment', part of Individuation Series by Michael Cook. It depicts a man, Joey, lying on a beach chair in the centre of the image. Over his body a woman has a tug of war with herself, a young man carries himself in the foreground, two men are tied together with ‘caution’ tape and on the jetty is Michael Cook himself, looking wistfully across the river while, in a boat in the river below, are two versions of his long term partner Monika Selig. artworks.title: 'Present' by Michael Cook
artworks.description: Photograph entitled 'Conformity', part of Individuation Series by Michael Cook. It depicts people walking across London Bridge, carrying placards as though protesting. Behind them Big Ben and other architectural icons represent colonisation and its pretentions to ‘civilisation’ while in the centre of the image, a man is knealing, Joey, and cooking a fish over a campfire. The clocks that bookend the bridge read 9 am on the left and 5 pm on the right, alluding to the workaday routine.

artworks.title: 'Narcissism' by Michael Cook
artworks.description: Photograph entitled 'Narcissism', part of Individuation Series by Michael Cook. It depicts a man, Joey, standing in front of Buckingham Palace wearing a floral suit and staring dreamily into space, unable to relate to the Western narcissistic tendencies in the women who surround him. Buckingham Palace is a dominant backdrop while, to either side, young women in Ophelia-like floral dresses stare into the pond’s reflection and mirrors, oblivious to everything outside their own image. artworks.title: 'Ego' by Michael Cook
artworks.description: Photograph entitled 'Narcissism', part of Individuation Series by Michael Cook. It depicts a man, Joey and a young woman crossing the road ahead of a line of luxury vehicles in front of Gucci and Balenciaga stores on the left and an entrance to Westminster Station on the right. Both Joey and the young woman are replicated many times in their gold designer fashion.

artworks.title: 'Energy' by Michael Cook
artworks.description: Photograph entitled 'Narcissism', part of Individuation Series by Michael Cook. It depicts a man, Joey, wearing a diamanté-encrusted suit, crouching on top of a train with rays of his torch shining out to connect with the individuals walking on the platform, symptomatic of the way he attracts people in his life, but also the power of our aura and energetic connections to people and place. artworks.title: 'Authenticity' by Michael Cook
artworks.description: Photograph entitled 'Narcissism', part of Individuation Series by Michael Cook. It depicts a man, Joey’s return home, his suit gradually sheds as he reunites with his Country. The horse walks with him, having abandoned the urban centre to remain with Joey, one of the camp dogs eats from the Balenciaga chip bag, mocking its iconic status in Western society and emphasising its redundancy in this outback environment.
